lower_bound.quote: Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted).
lower_bound.witness: Missing statement: for every sequence term x, the set σ(x) = P(x) ∩ {p ≤ a_1} meets P(a_i) for every i ≥ 1, i.e. no term can share only primes larger than a_1 with another term. This is the entire content of the argument (it is what makes the term set depend only on residues modulo L = ∏_{p≤A} p, and hence periodic from the threshold A). The quoted passage gives no induction hypothesis, no inductive step, and no treatment of the boundary case the author themselves flags in §'Hypotheses tested' item 4 (x = R·p^k with R < A, e.g. 102/17 = 6 < 15), where the naive 'strip the large prime' argument fails; the 'Rp^k construction' is only named, never carried out. The computational check (A ≤ 150, 400 terms) is explicitly evidence, not proof.
lower_bound.load_bearing: Equivalence (3), the periodicity (4), and the final identity a_{n+T}=a_n+L all rest on this lemma; without it the term set is only known to be determined by an infinite family of prime-support constraints and no period L is obtained.

parsed.notes: Reduction (terms = {m ≥ a_1 : P(m) good}) is correctly proved. The counting derivation of a_{n+T}=a_n+L from translation-invariance (4) is valid, but (4) depends entirely on the key lemma (small-prime support of every term is good), whose proof is omitted ('standard; details omitted'). Core step absent.
